301	def verify_pedersen_opening(
302	    commitment: PedersenCommitment,
303	    value: int,
304	    blinding: int,
305	) -> bool:
306	    """Verify that ``commitment`` opens at ``value`` with ``blinding``.
307	
308	    The group parameters and declared range come from ``commitment`` itself.
309	    A wrong object or field type raises :class:`TypeError`; an out-of-range
310	    element or value, or an incorrect opening, returns ``False``. Inputs are
311	    never mutated.
312	    """
313	    if not isinstance(commitment, PedersenCommitment):
314	        raise TypeError("commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
315	    for name in ("element", "lower", "upper", "prime", "generator", "h"):
316	        _check_int(getattr(commitment, name), f"commitment {name}")
317	    _check_int(value, "value")
318	    _check_int(blinding, "blinding")
319	    prime = commitment.prime
320	    if prime <= 3:
321	        return False
322	    if not 1 < commitment.generator < prime or not 1 < commitment.h < prime:
323	        return False
324	    if not 0 < commitment.element < prime:
325	        return False
326	    if commitment.lower > commitment.upper:
327	        return False
328	    if commitment.upper - commitment.lower >= prime - 1:
329	        return False
330	    if not commitment.lower <= value <= commitment.upper:
331	        return False
332	    if not 1 <= blinding < prime - 1:
333	        return False
334	    message = value - commitment.lower
335	    expected = (
336	        pow(commitment.generator, message, prime)
337	        * pow(commitment.h, blinding, prime)
338	        % prime
339	    )
340	    return expected == commitment.element
341	
342	
343	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
344	# Non-interactive Pedersen range proofs (Schnorr OR over the offsets)
345	#
346	# For each offset i in [0, n) define D_i = element * generator**(-i) mod prime.
347	# The commitment opens at value = lower + j with blinding r exactly when
348	# D_j = h**r, so a range proof is an OR proof: "I know the base-h discrete
349	# logarithm of at least one D_i". The real branch runs an honest Schnorr
350	# round; every other branch is simulated, and the Fiat-Shamir challenge
351	# shares are chosen so they sum to the transcript challenge modulo prime.
352	
353	_RANGE_DOMAIN = b"zkregion/pedersen-range/v1"
354	_MAX_RANGE_VALUES = 256
355	
356	
357	@dataclass(frozen=True)
358	class RangeProof:
359	    """A non-interactive range proof over a :class:`PedersenCommitment`.
360	
361	    ``t`` holds the per-branch announcements, ``e`` the challenge shares and
362	    ``s`` the responses; all three are tuples of ``upper - lower + 1``
363	    integers, one per integer in the declared range.
364	    """
365	
366	    t: tuple[int, ...]
367	    e: tuple[int, ...]
368	    s: tuple[int, ...]
369	
370	
371	def _range_challenge(
372	    commitment: PedersenCommitment,
373	    context: bytes,
374	    size: int,
375	    announcements: tuple[int, ...],
376	) -> int:
377	    """SHA-256 transcript challenge as a big-endian integer mod ``prime``.
378	
379	    The transcript is the domain separator, the six commitment fields, the
380	    context, the range size ``n`` and every announcement ``t_i``; each item
381	    is prefixed with its four-byte big-endian length and integers are
382	    encoded as decimal ASCII.
383	    """
384	    fields = (
385	        commitment.element,
386	        commitment.lower,
387	        commitment.upper,
388	        commitment.prime,
389	        commitment.generator,
390	        commitment.h,
391	    )
392	    items = [_RANGE_DOMAIN]
393	    items.extend(str(field).encode("ascii") for field in fields)
394	    items.append(context)
395	    items.append(str(size).encode("ascii"))
396	    items.extend(str(t).encode("ascii") for t in announcements)
397	    transcript = hashlib.sha256()
398	    for item in items:
399	        transcript.update(len(item).to_bytes(4, "big"))
400	        transcript.update(item)
401	    return int.from_bytes(transcript.digest(), "big") % commitment.prime
402	
403	
404	def _check_commitment_fields(commitment: PedersenCommitment) -> None:
405	    for name in ("element", "lower", "upper", "prime", "generator", "h"):
406	        _check_int(getattr(commitment, name), f"commitment {name}")
407	
408	
409	def prove_range(
410	    commitment: PedersenCommitment,
411	    value: int,
412	    blinding: int,
413	    context: bytes = b"",
414	    *,
415	    randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,
416	) -> RangeProof:
417	    """Prove that ``commitment`` opens at some value inside its declared range.
418	
419	    ``value`` and ``blinding`` must be a valid opening of ``commitment``;
420	    the opening is verified before any proving work happens and a mismatch
421	    raises :class:`ValueError`. The declared range may contain at most 256
422	    integers; wider ranges raise :class:`ValueError`. Randomness is drawn
423	    from ``randbelow`` (default :func:`secrets.randbelow`); a draw that is
424	    not a non-bool integer raises :class:`TypeError`, an out-of-range draw
425	    raises :class:`ValueError`.
426	    """
427	    if not isinstance(commitment, PedersenCommitment):
428	        raise TypeError("commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
429	    _check_commitment_fields(commitment)
430	    _check_int(value, "value")
431	    _check_int(blinding, "blinding")
432	    _check_bytes(context, "context")
433	    if not callable(randbelow):
434	        raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")
435	    size = commitment.upper - commitment.lower + 1
436	    if size > _MAX_RANGE_VALUES:
437	        raise ValueError(
438	            f"range must contain at most {_MAX_RANGE_VALUES} integers"
439	        )
440	    if not verify_pedersen_opening(commitment, value, blinding):
441	        raise ValueError("commitment does not open at (value, blinding)")
442	    prime = commitment.prime
443	    generator = commitment.generator
444	    h = commitment.h
445	
446	    def draw(upper: int) -> int:
447	        drawn = randbelow(upper)
448	        _check_int(drawn, "randbelow return value")
449	        if not 0 <= drawn < upper:
450	            raise ValueError(f"randbelow must return a value in [0, {upper})")
451	        return drawn
452	
453	    index = value - commitment.lower
454	    offsets = [commitment.element * pow(generator, -i, prime) % prime for i in range(size)]
455	    t: list[int] = [0] * size
456	    e: list[int] = [0] * size
457	    s: list[int] = [0] * size
458	    for i in range(size):
459	        if i == index:
460	            continue
461	        e[i] = draw(prime)  # challenge share in [0, prime)
462	        s[i] = draw(prime - 1) + 1  # non-negative response
463	        t[i] = pow(h, s[i], prime) * pow(offsets[i], -e[i], prime) % prime
464	    k = draw(prime - 1) + 1
465	    t[index] = pow(h, k, prime)
466	    challenge = _range_challenge(commitment, context, size, tuple(t))
467	    e[index] = (challenge - sum(e)) % prime
468	    s[index] = k + e[index] * blinding
469	    return RangeProof(t=tuple(t), e=tuple(e), s=tuple(s))
470	
471	
472	def verify_range(
473	    commitment: PedersenCommitment,
474	    proof: RangeProof,
475	    context: bytes = b"",
476	) -> bool:
477	    """Verify a :class:`RangeProof` against ``commitment`` and ``context``.
478	
479	    Every branch must satisfy the Schnorr equation
480	    ``h**s_i == t_i * D_i**e_i (mod prime)`` with
481	    ``D_i = element * generator**(-i) mod prime``, the challenge shares must
482	    lie in ``[0, prime)`` and sum to the transcript challenge modulo
483	    ``prime``, and the responses must be non-negative. Type errors (wrong
484	    object, non-tuple or non-integer proof fields, non-bytes context) raise
485	    :class:`TypeError`; any other invalid structure, tampering or binding
486	    mismatch — including ranges wider than 256 integers — returns ``False``.
487	    Inputs are never mutated.
488	    """
489	    if not isinstance(commitment, PedersenCommitment):
490	        raise TypeError("commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
491	    _check_commitment_fields(commitment)
492	    if not isinstance(proof, RangeProof):
493	        raise TypeError("proof must be a RangeProof")
494	    for field_name in ("t", "e", "s"):
495	        field = getattr(proof, field_name)
496	        if not isinstance(field, tuple):
497	            raise TypeError(f"proof {field_name} must be a tuple of integers")
498	        for item in field:
499	            _check_int(item, f"proof {field_name} entry")
500	    _check_bytes(context, "context")
501	    prime = commitment.prime
502	    if prime <= 3:
503	        return False
504	    if not 1 < commitment.generator < prime or not 1 < commitment.h < prime:
505	        return False
506	    if not 0 < commitment.element < prime:
507	        return False
508	    if commitment.lower > commitment.upper:
509	        return False
510	    if commitment.upper - commitment.lower >= prime - 1:
511	        return False
512	    size = commitment.upper - commitment.lower + 1
513	    if size > _MAX_RANGE_VALUES:
514	        return False
515	    if not (len(proof.t) == len(proof.e) == len(proof.s) == size):
516	        return False
517	    if any(not 1 <= t_i < prime for t_i in proof.t):
518	        return False
519	    if any(not 0 <= e_i < prime for e_i in proof.e):
520	        return False
521	    if any(s_i < 0 for s_i in proof.s):
522	        return False
523	    challenge = _range_challenge(commitment, context, size, proof.t)
524	    if sum(proof.e) % prime != challenge:
525	        return False
526	    generator = commitment.generator
527	    h = commitment.h
528	    try:
529	        inverses = [pow(generator, -i, prime) for i in range(size)]
530	    except ValueError:
531	        return False  # generator not invertible modulo prime
532	    for i in range(size):
533	        offset = commitment.element * inverses[i] % prime
534	        left = pow(h, proof.s[i], prime)
535	        right = proof.t[i] * pow(offset, proof.e[i], prime) % prime
536	        if left != right:
537	            return False
538	    return True
539

541	@dataclass(frozen=True)
542	class RangeBatchEntry:
543	    """One item of a range batch verification.
544	
545	    Fields are the :class:`PedersenCommitment`, the :class:`RangeProof` and
546	    the ``context`` (empty by default) — exactly the arguments of
547	    :func:`verify_range`, in the same order.
548	    """
549	
550	    commitment: PedersenCommitment
551	    proof: RangeProof
552	    context: bytes = b""
553	
554	
555	def verify_range_batch(
556	    entries: Sequence[RangeBatchEntry],
557	    *,
558	    randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,
559	) -> bool:
560	    """Verify a batch of :class:`RangeProof` objects with random linear checks.
561	
562	    ``entries`` must be a non-empty, non-string sequence of
563	    :class:`RangeBatchEntry`; an empty batch returns ``False`` and
564	    duplicate entries are legal (each draws its own coefficients). Every
565	    entry reuses the established :class:`RangeProof` transcript byte for
566	    byte, binding the six commitment fields, the declared range and the
567	    ``context``: the proof structure and tuple sizes must match, the
568	    ``t`` / ``e`` / ``s`` values must be in range, and the challenge
569	    shares must sum to the transcript challenge.
570	
571	    Each range-proof branch then draws exactly one random coefficient
572	    ``a = r + 1`` with ``r = randbelow(prime - 1)``. Branches sharing the
573	    same ``(prime, generator, h)`` group are checked together with a
574	    single aggregate equation
575	
576	    ``h**Σ(a*s) == Π(t**a * D_i**(a*e)) (mod prime)``
577	
578	    where ``D_i = element * generator**(-i) mod prime`` is unchanged from
579	    :func:`verify_range`; per-branch results are never AND-ed together.
580	    Type errors — including ``bool`` integers and a non-callable
581	    ``randbelow`` or one that returns a non-integer — raise
582	    :class:`TypeError`; a coefficient outside ``[0, prime - 1)`` raises
583	    :class:`ValueError`. Every other invalid structure, tampering,
584	    commitment or context binding mismatch returns ``False``;
585	    short-circuiting is allowed. Missing entries cannot be detected: the
586	    caller guarantees the batch is complete. Inputs are never mutated.
587	    """
588	    if isinstance(entries, (bytes, bytearray, str)) or not isinstance(entries, Sequence):
589	        raise TypeError("entries must be a sequence of RangeBatchEntry")
590	    if not callable(randbelow):
591	        raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")
592	    items = list(entries)  # copy: inputs are never mutated
593	    if not items:
594	        return False
595	
596	    # group -> {"sum": Σ(a*s), "product": Π(t**a * D_i**(a*e))}
597	    groups: dict[tuple[int, int, int], dict[str, int]] = {}
598	
599	    def add_branch(
600	        group_key: tuple[int, int, int],
601	        t_i: int,
602	        e_i: int,
603	        s_i: int,
604	        offset_i: int,
605	    ) -> None:
606	        prime, _generator, _h = group_key
607	        r = randbelow(prime - 1)
608	        if not isinstance(r, int) or isinstance(r, bool):
609	            raise TypeError("coefficient source randbelow must return an integer")
610	        if not 0 <= r < prime - 1:
611	            raise ValueError("coefficient source must satisfy 0 <= r < prime - 1")
612	        coefficient = r + 1
613	        state = groups.setdefault(group_key, {"sum": 0, "product": 1})
614	        state["sum"] += coefficient * s_i
615	        state["product"] = (
616	            state["product"]
617	            * pow(t_i, coefficient, prime)
618	            % prime
619	            * pow(offset_i, coefficient * e_i, prime)
620	            % prime
621	        )
622	
623	    for position, entry in enumerate(items):
624	        if not isinstance(entry, RangeBatchEntry):
625	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] must be a RangeBatchEntry")
626	        commitment = entry.commitment
627	        proof = entry.proof
628	        if not isinstance(commitment, PedersenCommitment):
629	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
630	        _check_commitment_fields(commitment)
631	        if not isinstance(proof, RangeProof):
632	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] proof must be a RangeProof")
633	        for field_name in ("t", "e", "s"):
634	            field = getattr(proof, field_name)
635	            if not isinstance(field, tuple):
636	                raise TypeError(
637	                    f"entries[{position}] proof {field_name} must be a tuple of integers"
638	                )
639	            for item in field:
640	                _check_int(item, f"entries[{position}] proof {field_name} entry")
641	        _check_bytes(entry.context, f"entries[{position}] context")
642	        try:
643	            prime, generator, h, size, announcements, shares, responses = (
644	                _range_proof_check_material(commitment, proof, entry.context)
645	            )
646	            inverses = [pow(generator, -i, prime) for i in range(size)]
647	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
648	            return False  # structural/transcript mismatch: short-circuit
649	        group_key = (prime, generator, h)
650	        for i in range(size):
651	            offset_i = commitment.element * inverses[i] % prime
652	            add_branch(
653	                group_key,
654	                announcements[i],
655	                shares[i],
656	                responses[i],
657	                offset_i,
658	            )
659	
660	    for (prime, _generator, _h), state in groups.items():
661	        if pow(_h, state["sum"], prime) != state["product"]:
662	            return False
663	    return True

666	class SchnorrProver:
667	    """Interactive Schnorr prover over a multiplicative group."""
668	
669	    def __init__(
670	        self,
671	        secret: int,
672	        *,
673	        prime: int = DEFAULT_PRIME,
674	        generator: int = DEFAULT_GENERATOR,
675	        randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,
676	    ) -> None:
677	        if not isinstance(secret, int):
678	            raise TypeError("secret must be an integer")
679	        if not 0 < secret < prime:
680	            raise ValueError("secret must satisfy 0 < secret < prime")
681	        if not 1 < generator < prime:
682	            raise ValueError("generator must satisfy 1 < generator < prime")
683	        self._secret = secret
684	        self._prime = prime
685	        self._generator = generator
686	        self._randbelow = randbelow
687	        self._nonce: int | None = None
688	
689	    @property
690	    def prime(self) -> int:
691	        return self._prime
692	
693	    @property
694	    def generator(self) -> int:
695	        return self._generator
696	
697	    @property
698	    def public_key(self) -> int:
699	        return pow(self._generator, self._secret, self._prime)
700	
701	    def new_commitment(self) -> int:
702	        """Draw a fresh nonce and publish ``g**k mod prime``."""
703	        self._nonce = self._randbelow(self._prime - 1) + 1
704	        return pow(self._generator, self._nonce, self._prime)
705	
706	    def respond(self, challenge: int) -> int:
707	        """Answer the verifier's challenge for the most recent commitment."""
708	        if self._nonce is None:
709	            raise RuntimeError("call new_commitment() before respond()")
710	        if not isinstance(challenge, int):
711	            raise TypeError("challenge must be an integer")
712	        bounded = challenge % self._prime
713	        return self._nonce + bounded * self._secret
714	
715	    def prove(self, message: bytes, *, context: bytes = b"") -> SchnorrProof:
716	        """Non-interactive Fiat-Shamir proof of knowledge of the secret.
717	
718	        Draws a fresh ephemeral ``k`` independently of the interactive nonce
719	        and returns ``SchnorrProof(t, s)`` with ``s = k + c * secret`` (not
720	        reduced modulo the group order).
721	        """
722	        _check_bytes(message, "message")
723	        _check_bytes(context, "context")
724	        k = self._randbelow(self._prime - 1) + 1
725	        commitment = pow(self._generator, k, self._prime)
726	        challenge = _fs_challenge(
727	            self._prime, self._generator, self.public_key, commitment, context, message
728	        )
729	        return SchnorrProof(commitment=commitment, response=k + challenge * self._secret)

732	class SchnorrVerifier:
733	    """Checks the Schnorr response against a published commitment."""
734	
735	    def __init__(self, public_key: int, *, prime: int = DEFAULT_PRIME, generator: int = DEFAULT_GENERATOR) -> None:
736	        if not isinstance(public_key, int):
737	            raise TypeError("public_key must be an integer")
738	        if not 0 < public_key < prime:
739	            raise ValueError("public_key must satisfy 0 < public_key < prime")
740	        if not 1 < generator < prime:
741	            raise ValueError("generator must satisfy 1 < generator < prime")
742	        self._public_key = public_key
743	        self._prime = prime
744	        self._generator = generator

746	    @property
747	    def public_key(self) -> int:
748	        return self._public_key

750	    def verify(self, commitment: int, challenge: int, response: int) -> bool:
751	        for value in (commitment, challenge, response):
752	            if not isinstance(value, int):
753	                raise TypeError("commitment, challenge and response must be integers")
754	        bounded = challenge % self._prime
755	        left = pow(self._generator, response, self._prime)
756	        right = commitment * pow(self._public_key, bounded, self._prime) % self._prime
757	        return left == right

759	    def verify_proof(self, message: bytes, proof: SchnorrProof, *, context: bytes = b"") -> bool:
760	        """Check a Fiat-Shamir proof produced by :meth:`SchnorrProver.prove`."""
761	        _check_bytes(message, "message")
762	        _check_bytes(context, "context")
763	        if not isinstance(proof, SchnorrProof):
764	            raise TypeError("proof must be a SchnorrProof")
765	        if not isinstance(proof.commitment, int) or not isinstance(proof.response, int):
766	            raise TypeError("proof commitment and response must be integers")
767	        if not 1 <= proof.commitment < self._prime or proof.response < 0:
768	            return False
769	        challenge = _fs_challenge(
770	            self._prime, self._generator, self._public_key, proof.commitment, context, message
771	        )
772	        left = pow(self._generator, proof.response, self._prime)
773	        right = proof.commitment * pow(self._public_key, challenge, self._prime) % self._prime
774	        return left == right

776	    def verify_batch(
777	        self,
778	        entries: Sequence[SchnorrBatchEntry],
779	        *,
780	        randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,

782	        """Verify a batch of Fiat-Shamir proofs made for this public key.
783	
784	        Every structurally valid entry recomputes its transcript challenge
785	        ``c`` and draws exactly one coefficient ``a = r + 1`` from
786	        ``r = randbelow(prime - 1)``; the batch is accepted iff the random
787	        linear combination ``g**Σ(a*s) == Π(t**a * public_key**(a*c))``
788	        holds modulo ``prime`` — never a per-entry boolean summary. An
789	        empty batch returns False; out-of-range commitments, negative
790	        responses, mismatched messages or contexts and any tampering
791	        return False, and an invalid proof may short-circuit the batch.
792	        Duplicate entries are legal and each draws its own coefficient.
793	        A fixed ``randbelow`` makes the result reproducible; the default
794	        is :func:`secrets.randbelow`.
795	        """
796	        if isinstance(entries, (bytes, bytearray, str)) or not isinstance(entries, Sequence):
797	            raise TypeError("entries must be a sequence of SchnorrBatchEntry")
798	        if not callable(randbelow):
799	            raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")
800	        items = list(entries)  # copy: inputs are never mutated
801	        if not items:
802	            return False
803	        exponent_sum = 0
804	        product = 1
805	        for position, entry in enumerate(items):
806	            if not isinstance(entry, SchnorrBatchEntry):
807	                raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] must be a SchnorrBatchEntry")
808	            _check_bytes(entry.message, f"entries[{position}] message")
809	            _check_bytes(entry.context, f"entries[{position}] context")
810	            proof = entry.proof
811	            if not isinstance(proof, SchnorrProof):
812	                raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] proof must be a SchnorrProof")
813	            if (
814	                not isinstance(proof.commitment, int)
815	                or isinstance(proof.commitment, bool)
816	                or not isinstance(proof.response, int)
817	                or isinstance(proof.response, bool)
818	            ):
819	                raise TypeError(
820	                    f"entries[{position}] proof commitment and response must be integers"
821	                )
822	            if not 1 <= proof.commitment < self._prime or proof.response < 0:
823	                return False  # structurally invalid proof: short-circuit
824	            challenge = _fs_challenge(
825	                self._prime,
826	                self._generator,
827	                self._public_key,
828	                proof.commitment,
829	                entry.context,
830	                entry.message,
831	            )
832	            r = randbelow(self._prime - 1)
833	            if not isinstance(r, int) or isinstance(r, bool):
834	                raise TypeError("coefficient source randbelow must return an integer")
835	            if not 0 <= r < self._prime - 1:
836	                raise ValueError("coefficient source must satisfy 0 <= r < prime - 1")
837	            coefficient = r + 1
838	            exponent_sum += coefficient * proof.response
839	            product = product * pow(proof.commitment, coefficient, self._prime) % self._prime
840	            product = (
841	                product

858	    must be a non-empty, non-string sequence of :class:`MultiSchnorrEntry`;
859	    an empty batch returns ``False`` and duplicate entries are legal (each

863	    ``message``, ``proof``, ``context``, ``prime`` and ``generator``.

866	    ``a = r + 1`` with ``r = randbelow(prime - 1)``. Entries sharing the
867	    same ``(prime, generator)`` group are checked together with a single
868	    aggregate equation
869	
870	    ``g**Σ(a*s) == Π(t**a * public_key**(a*c)) (mod prime)``
871	
872	    with each entry contributing under its own ``public_key``; per-entry
873	    results are never AND-ed together, and errors cannot cancel across
874	    different groups. Type errors — including ``bool`` integers and a
875	    non-callable ``randbelow`` or one that returns a non-integer — raise
876	    :class:`TypeError`; a coefficient outside ``[0, prime - 1)`` raises
877	    :class:`ValueError`. Every other invalid structure, tampering or
878	    binding mismatch returns ``False``; short-circuiting is allowed.
879	    Missing entries cannot be detected: the caller guarantees the batch
880	    is complete. Inputs are never mutated.

885	        raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")

887	    if not items:
888	        return False
889	
890	    # (prime, generator) -> {"sum": Σ(a*s), "product": Π(t**a * y**(a*c))}
891	    groups: dict[tuple[int, int], dict[str, int]] = {}
892	
893	    for position, entry in enumerate(items):
894	        if not isinstance(entry, MultiSchnorrEntry):
895	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] must be a MultiSchnorrEntry")

918	            return False
919	        if not 1 <= proof.commitment < prime or proof.response < 0:

923	            generator,
924	            entry.public_key,
925	            proof.commitment,
926	            entry.context,
927	            entry.message,
928	        )

982	# Non-interactive 2-D region membership proofs
983	#
984	# A region proof is a pair of Pedersen range proofs, one per axis: the x
985	# commitment must be declared over exactly [region.min_x, region.max_x] and
986	# the y commitment over exactly [region.min_y, region.max_y]. Each sub-proof
987	# is produced by prove_range under a derived context that binds the region
988	# domain separator, the axis label, the external context, the four region
989	# bounds and both commitments, so a proof cannot be replayed against another
990	# region, context, commitment pair or axis assignment.
991	
992	_REGION_DOMAIN = b"zkregion/region/v1"

995	@dataclass(frozen=True)
996	class RegionProof:
997	    """A non-interactive 2-D region membership proof.
998	
999	    ``x_proof`` and ``y_proof`` are :class:`RangeProof` objects over the x
1000	    and y :class:`PedersenCommitment` respectively; the verifier learns
1001	    nothing about the coordinates or blinding factors.
1002	    """
1003	
1004	    x_proof: RangeProof
1005	    y_proof: RangeProof
1006

1008	def _check_region_fields(region: Region) -> None:
1009	    for name in ("min_x", "max_x", "min_y", "max_y"):
1010	        _check_int(getattr(region, name), f"region {name}")

1013	def _region_sub_context(
1014	    axis: bytes,
1015	    context: bytes,
1016	    region: Region,
1017	    x_commitment: PedersenCommitment,
1018	    y_commitment: PedersenCommitment,
1019	) -> bytes:
1020	    """Length-prefixed transcript context for one axis sub-proof.
1021	
1022	    Items, in order: the region domain separator, the axis label, the
1023	    external context, the four region bounds and the six fields of the x
1024	    then the y commitment (dataclass field order). Every item is prefixed
1025	    with its four-byte unsigned big-endian length; integers are encoded as
1026	    decimal ASCII.
1027	    """
1028	    items = [_REGION_DOMAIN, axis, context]
1029	    items.extend(
1030	        str(bound).encode("ascii")
1031	        for bound in (region.min_x, region.max_x, region.min_y, region.max_y)
1032	    )
1033	    for commitment in (x_commitment, y_commitment):
1034	        items.extend(
1035	            str(getattr(commitment, name)).encode("ascii")
1036	            for name in ("element", "lower", "upper", "prime", "generator", "h")
1037	        )
1038	    transcript = bytearray()
1039	    for item in items:
1040	        transcript += len(item).to_bytes(4, "big")
1041	        transcript += item
1042	    return bytes(transcript)

1045	def prove_region(
1046	    x_commitment: PedersenCommitment,
1047	    y_commitment: PedersenCommitment,
1048	    x: int,
1049	    y: int,
1050	    x_blinding: int,
1051	    y_blinding: int,
1052	    region: Region,
1053	    context: bytes = b"",
1054	    *,
1055	    randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,
1056	) -> RegionProof:
1057	    """Prove that the committed ``(x, y)`` lies inside ``region``.
1058	
1059	    ``x_commitment`` must be declared over exactly
1060	    ``[region.min_x, region.max_x]`` and ``y_commitment`` over exactly
1061	    ``[region.min_y, region.max_y]``; a mismatch raises :class:`ValueError`.
1062	    Each opening is verified (via :func:`prove_range`) before its sub-proof
1063	    is produced, and each axis range may contain at most 256 integers —
1064	    violations raise :class:`ValueError`. Type errors (wrong objects,
1065	    non-integer or ``bool`` numbers, non-``bytes`` context, non-callable
1066	    ``randbelow``) raise :class:`TypeError`. Inputs are never mutated.
1067	    """
1068	    if not isinstance(x_commitment, PedersenCommitment):
1069	        raise TypeError("x_commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
1070	    if not isinstance(y_commitment, PedersenCommitment):
1071	        raise TypeError("y_commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
1072	    _check_commitment_fields(x_commitment)
1073	    _check_commitment_fields(y_commitment)
1074	    _check_int(x, "x")
1075	    _check_int(y, "y")
1076	    _check_int(x_blinding, "x_blinding")
1077	    _check_int(y_blinding, "y_blinding")
1078	    if not isinstance(region, Region):
1079	        raise TypeError("region must be a Region")
1080	    _check_region_fields(region)
1081	    _check_bytes(context, "context")
1082	    if not callable(randbelow):
1083	        raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")
1084	    if (x_commitment.lower, x_commitment.upper) != (region.min_x, region.max_x):
1085	        raise ValueError("x commitment range must equal (region.min_x, region.max_x)")
1086	    if (y_commitment.lower, y_commitment.upper) != (region.min_y, region.max_y):
1087	        raise ValueError("y commitment range must equal (region.min_y, region.max_y)")
1088	    x_proof = prove_range(
1089	        x_commitment,
1090	        x,
1091	        x_blinding,
1092	        _region_sub_context(b"x", context, region, x_commitment, y_commitment),
1093	        randbelow=randbelow,
1094	    )
1095	    y_proof = prove_range(
1096	        y_commitment,
1097	        y,
1098	        y_blinding,
1099	        _region_sub_context(b"y", context, region, x_commitment, y_commitment),

1169	def _range_proof_check_material(

1172	    context: bytes,
1173	) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:

1180	    ``(prime, generator, h, size, t, e, s)``; ``D_i`` is recomputed by the
1181	    caller as ``element * generator**(-i) mod prime``.

1183	    prime = commitment.prime
1184	    generator = commitment.generator
1185	    h = commitment.h
1186	    if prime <= 3 or not 1 < generator < prime or not 1 < h < prime:
1187	        raise ValueError("invalid commitment group parameters")
1188	    if not 0 < commitment.element < prime:
1189	        raise ValueError("commitment element out of range")
1190	    if commitment.lower > commitment.upper:
1191	        raise ValueError("commitment lower must not exceed upper")
1192	    if commitment.upper - commitment.lower >= prime - 1:

1194	    size = commitment.upper - commitment.lower + 1
1195	    if size > _MAX_RANGE_VALUES:
1196	        raise ValueError(f"range must contain at most {_MAX_RANGE_VALUES} integers")

1200	        raise ValueError("proof announcement out of range")

1202	        raise ValueError("proof challenge share out of range")

1211	def verify_region_batch(
1212	    entries: Sequence[RegionBatchEntry],
1213	    *,
1214	    randbelow: Callable[[int], int] = secrets.randbelow,
1215	) -> bool:
1216	    """Verify a batch of :class:`RegionProof` objects with random linear checks.
1217	
1218	    ``entries`` must be a non-empty, non-string sequence of
1219	    :class:`RegionBatchEntry`; an empty batch returns ``False`` and
1220	    duplicate entries are legal (each draws its own coefficients). Every
1221	    entry is validated exactly as :func:`verify_region` would, reusing the
1222	    established :class:`Region` and :class:`RangeProof` transcripts
1223	    byte for byte: the commitment ranges must equal the region bounds, the
1224	    sub-proof structure and tuple sizes must match, the ``t`` / ``e`` /
1225	    ``s`` values must be in range, and the challenge shares must sum to
1226	    the transcript challenge.
1227	
1228	    Each range-proof branch then draws exactly one random coefficient
1229	    ``a = r + 1`` with ``r = randbelow(prime - 1)``. Branches sharing the
1230	    same ``(prime, generator, h)`` group are checked together with a
1231	    single aggregate equation
1232	
1233	    ``h**Σ(a*s) == Π(t**a * D_i**(a*e)) (mod prime)``
1234	
1235	    where ``D_i = element * generator**(-i) mod prime`` is unchanged from
1236	    :func:`verify_range`; per-branch results are never AND-ed together.
1237	    Type errors — including ``bool`` integers and a non-callable
1238	    ``randbelow`` or one that returns a non-integer — raise
1239	    :class:`TypeError`; a coefficient outside ``[0, prime - 1)`` raises
1240	    :class:`ValueError`. Every other invalid structure, tampering, region,
1241	    commitment or context binding mismatch, cross-item recombination or
1242	    sub-proof count error returns ``False``; short-circuiting is allowed.
1243	    Missing entries cannot be detected: the caller guarantees the batch
1244	    is complete. Inputs are never mutated.
1245	    """
1246	    if isinstance(entries, (bytes, bytearray, str)) or not isinstance(entries, Sequence):
1247	        raise TypeError("entries must be a sequence of RegionBatchEntry")
1248	    if not callable(randbelow):
1249	        raise TypeError("randbelow must be callable")
1250	    items = list(entries)  # copy: inputs are never mutated
1251	    if not items:
1252	        return False
1253	
1254	    # group -> {"sum": Σ(a*s), "product": Π(t**a * D_i**(a*e))}
1255	    groups: dict[tuple[int, int, int], dict[str, int]] = {}
1256	
1257	    def add_branch(
1258	        group_key: tuple[int, int, int],
1259	        t_i: int,
1260	        e_i: int,
1261	        s_i: int,
1262	        offset_i: int,
1263	    ) -> None:
1264	        prime, _generator, _h = group_key
1265	        r = randbelow(prime - 1)
1266	        if not isinstance(r, int) or isinstance(r, bool):
1267	            raise TypeError("coefficient source randbelow must return an integer")
1268	        if not 0 <= r < prime - 1:
1269	            raise ValueError("coefficient source must satisfy 0 <= r < prime - 1")
1270	        coefficient = r + 1
1271	        state = groups.setdefault(group_key, {"sum": 0, "product": 1})
1272	        state["sum"] += coefficient * s_i
1273	        state["product"] = (
1274	            state["product"]
1275	            * pow(t_i, coefficient, prime)
1276	            % prime
1277	            * pow(offset_i, coefficient * e_i, prime)
1278	            % prime
1279	        )
1280	
1281	    for position, entry in enumerate(items):
1282	        if not isinstance(entry, RegionBatchEntry):
1283	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] must be a RegionBatchEntry")
1284	        x_commitment = entry.x_commitment
1285	        y_commitment = entry.y_commitment
1286	        region = entry.region
1287	        proof = entry.proof
1288	        if not isinstance(x_commitment, PedersenCommitment):
1289	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] x_commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")
1290	        if not isinstance(y_commitment, PedersenCommitment):
1291	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] y_commitment must be a PedersenCommitment")

1293	        _check_commitment_fields(y_commitment)
1294	        if not isinstance(region, Region):
1295	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] region must be a Region")
1296	        _check_region_fields(region)
1297	        if not isinstance(proof, RegionProof):
1298	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] proof must be a RegionProof")
1299	        if not isinstance(proof.x_proof, RangeProof):
1300	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] proof x_proof must be a RangeProof")
1301	        if not isinstance(proof.y_proof, RangeProof):
1302	            raise TypeError(f"entries[{position}] proof y_proof must be a RangeProof")
1303	        for axis_name, sub_proof in (("x", proof.x_proof), ("y", proof.y_proof)):
1304	            for field_name in ("t", "e", "s"):
1305	                field = getattr(sub_proof, field_name)

1314	                        f"entries[{position}] {axis_name}_proof {field_name} entry",
1315	                    )

1318	            return False
1319	        if (y_commitment.lower, y_commitment.upper) != (region.min_y, region.max_y):
1320	            return False
1321	        axes = (
1322	            (
1323	                b"x",
1324	                x_commitment,
1325	                proof.x_proof,
1326	                _region_sub_context(b"x", entry.context, region, x_commitment, y_commitment),
1327	            ),
1328	            (
1329	                b"y",
1330	                y_commitment,
1331	                proof.y_proof,
1332	                _region_sub_context(b"y", entry.context, region, x_commitment, y_commitment),
1333	            ),

1335	        for _axis, commitment, sub_proof, sub_context in axes:
1336	            try:
1337	                prime, generator, h, size, announcements, shares, responses = (

1361	# Deterministic SHA-256 Merkle inclusion proofs
1362	#
1363	# Leaf digest:     SHA-256(b"\x00" + len4 + leaf)   (len4 = 4-byte BE length)
1364	# Internal digest: SHA-256(b"\x01" + left + right)
1365	# Layers pair nodes in input order; an odd node is duplicated before merging.
1366	# A single-leaf tree's root is the leaf digest and its proof path is empty.
1367	
1368	_MERKLE_LEAF_PREFIX = b"\x00"
1369	_MERKLE_NODE_PREFIX = b"\x01"
1370	_MERKLE_DIGEST_SIZE = 32
1371	
1372	
1373	@dataclass(frozen=True)
1374	class MerkleProof:
1375	    """Inclusion proof: zero-based leaf ``index`` and ``siblings`` from leaf to root."""
1376	
1377	    index: int
1378	    siblings: tuple[bytes, ...]
1379	
1380	
1381	def _leaf_digest(leaf: bytes) -> bytes:
1382	    return hashlib.sha256(
1383	        _MERKLE_LEAF_PREFIX + len(leaf).to_bytes(4, "big") + leaf
1384	    ).digest()
1385	
1386	
1387	def _node_digest(left: bytes, right: bytes) -> bytes:
1388	    return hashlib.sha256(_MERKLE_NODE_PREFIX + left + right).digest()
1389	
1390	
1391	def _checked_leaves(leaves: Sequence[bytes]) -> list[bytes]:
1392	    if isinstance(leaves, (bytes, bytearray, str)) or not isinstance(leaves, Sequence):
1393	        raise TypeError("leaves must be a sequence of bytes")
1394	    items = list(leaves)  # copy: inputs are never mutated
1395	    if not items:
1396	        raise ValueError("leaves must not be empty")
1397	    for position, leaf in enumerate(items):
1398	        if not isinstance(leaf, bytes):
1399	            raise TypeError(f"leaves[{position}] must be bytes")
1400	    return items
1401	
1402	
1403	def _check_merkle_index(index: int, size: int) -> None:
1404	    if not isinstance(index, int) or isinstance(index, bool):
1405	        raise TypeError("index must be an integer")
1406	    if not 0 <= index < size:
1407	        raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range for {size} leaves")
1408	
1409	
1410	def merkle_root(leaves: Sequence[bytes]) -> bytes:
1411	    """Return the Merkle root digest of a non-empty sequence of byte leaves."""
1412	    level = [_leaf_digest(leaf) for leaf in _checked_leaves(leaves)]
1413	    while len(level) > 1:
1414	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
1415	            level = level + [level[-1]]
1416	        level = [
1417	            _node_digest(level[offset], level[offset + 1])
1418	            for offset in range(0, len(level), 2)
1419	        ]
1420	    return level[0]
1421	
1422	
1423	def prove_inclusion(leaves: Sequence[bytes], index: int) -> MerkleProof:
1424	    """Build a :class:`MerkleProof` for the leaf at zero-based ``index``.
1425	
1426	    Duplicate leaves are located purely by position; content is never searched.
1427	    """
1428	    items = _checked_leaves(leaves)
1429	    _check_merkle_index(index, len(items))
1430	    level = [_leaf_digest(leaf) for leaf in items]
1431	    siblings: list[bytes] = []
1432	    position = index
1433	    while len(level) > 1:
1434	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
1435	            level = level + [level[-1]]
1436	        siblings.append(level[position ^ 1])
1437	        level = [
1438	            _node_digest(level[offset], level[offset + 1])
1439	            for offset in range(0, len(level), 2)
1440	        ]
1441	        position //= 2
1442	    return MerkleProof(index=index, siblings=tuple(siblings))

1445	def verify_inclusion(leaf: bytes, proof: MerkleProof, root: bytes) -> bool:
1446	    """Check that ``leaf`` sits at ``proof.index`` under Merkle ``root``.
1447	
1448	    Type errors raise :class:`TypeError`; malformed digest lengths or an
1449	    index/path structure that cannot correspond to a real tree return False.
1450	    """
1451	    _check_bytes(leaf, "leaf")
1452	    _check_bytes(root, "root")
1453	    if not isinstance(proof, MerkleProof):
1454	        raise TypeError("proof must be a MerkleProof")
1455	    if not isinstance(proof.index, int) or isinstance(proof.index, bool):
1456	        raise TypeError("proof index must be an integer")
1457	    if not isinstance(proof.siblings, tuple):
1458	        raise TypeError("proof siblings must be a tuple of bytes")
1459	    for sibling in proof.siblings:
1460	        _check_bytes(sibling, "proof sibling")
1461	    if len(root) != _MERKLE_DIGEST_SIZE:
1462	        return False
1463	    if proof.index < 0:
1464	        return False
1465	    if any(len(sibling) != _MERKLE_DIGEST_SIZE for sibling in proof.siblings):
1466	        return False
1467	    digest = _leaf_digest(leaf)
1468	    position = proof.index
1469	    for sibling in proof.siblings:
1470	        if position % 2 == 0:
1471	            digest = _node_digest(digest, sibling)
1472	        else:
1473	            digest = _node_digest(sibling, digest)
1474	        position //= 2
1475	    if position != 0:
1476	        return False  # index deeper than the path allows
1477	    return hmac.compare_digest(digest, root)

1481	# Compact Merkle multi-inclusion proofs
1482	#
1483	# Same digests and odd-node duplication as the single-leaf proofs above, but
1484	# one proof covers several leaves at once: siblings shared by two proven
1485	# nodes are collected only once, and a sibling that is itself proven (or an
1486	# odd last node that duplicates itself) is never collected at all.
1487	
1488	
1489	@dataclass(frozen=True)
1490	class MerkleMultiProof:
1491	    """Multi-inclusion proof for ``indices`` within ``leaf_count`` leaves.
1492	
1493	    ``siblings`` lists the digests the verifier cannot recompute, ordered
1494	    level by level from leaf to root and left to right within each level.
1495	    """
1496	
1497	    leaf_count: int
1498	    indices: tuple[int, ...]
1499	    siblings: tuple[bytes, ...]
1500	
1501	
1502	def _checked_multi_indices(indices: Sequence[int], size: int) -> list[int]:
1503	    if isinstance(indices, (bytes, bytearray, str)) or not isinstance(indices, Sequence):
1504	        raise TypeError("indices must be a sequence of integers")
1505	    items = list(indices)  # copy: inputs are never mutated
1506	    if not items:
1507	        raise ValueError("indices must not be empty")
1508	    previous: int | None = None
1509	    for position, index in enumerate(items):
1510	        if not isinstance(index, int) or isinstance(index, bool):
1511	            raise TypeError(f"indices[{position}] must be an integer")
1512	        if previous is not None and index <= previous:
1513	            raise ValueError("indices must be strictly increasing without duplicates")
1514	        previous = index
1515	    for index in items:
1516	        if not 0 <= index < size:
1517	            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range for {size} leaves")
1518	    return items
1519	
1520	
1521	def prove_multi_inclusion(leaves: Sequence[bytes], indices: Sequence[int]) -> MerkleMultiProof:
1522	    """Build a compact :class:`MerkleMultiProof` for the leaves at ``indices``.
1523	
1524	    ``indices`` must be non-empty, strictly increasing and duplicate-free.
1525	    The proof is deterministic and minimal: when every leaf is proven,
1526	    ``siblings`` is empty.
1527	    """
1528	    items = _checked_leaves(leaves)
1529	    positions = _checked_multi_indices(indices, len(items))
1530	    level = [_leaf_digest(leaf) for leaf in items]
1531	    siblings: list[bytes] = []
1532	    known = positions
1533	    while len(level) > 1:
1534	        size = len(level)
1535	        known_set = set(known)
1536	        for position in known:  # ascending: siblings collected left to right
1537	            sibling = position ^ 1
1538	            if sibling in known_set:
1539	                continue  # sibling is proven too, nothing to collect
1540	            if position == size - 1 and size % 2 == 1:
1541	                continue  # odd last node duplicates itself
1542	            siblings.append(level[sibling])
1543	        if size % 2 == 1:
1544	            level = level + [level[-1]]
1545	        level = [
1546	            _node_digest(level[offset], level[offset + 1])
1547	            for offset in range(0, len(level), 2)
1548	        ]
1549	        known = sorted({position // 2 for position in known})
1550	    return MerkleMultiProof(
1551	        leaf_count=len(items),
1552	        indices=tuple(positions),
1553	        siblings=tuple(siblings),
1554	    )
1555

1557	def verify_multi_inclusion(
1558	    entries: Sequence[tuple[int, bytes]],

1564	    ``entries`` holds one ``(index, leaf)`` pair per entry, in the exact order
1565	    of ``proof.indices``. Type errors raise :class:`TypeError`; empty,
1566	    misordered, out-of-range, miscounted or tampered inputs return False.

1572	        raise TypeError("proof leaf_count must be an integer")

Public API: commit / verify_opening / commit_coordinate / PedersenCommitment /
